text: Code refactoring means improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read and understand. When developers refactor, they clean up messy sections, remove duplicate parts, and give variables clearer names. The program should still work exactly the same way after refactoring. This practice helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes and poor solutions are used. By refactoring regularly, teams keep their code healthy and easier to maintain in the future.
